newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria nosedive comes to a halt in Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria nosedive comes to a halt in Brady market.

text.p: The slump in Bulgarian Brady bonds came to an end on Thursday after the previous day's panic selling on warnings of possible default, but traders said it will remain unsteady until the country resolves its problems.
Bulgarian IABs tumbled more than two points on Wednesday after President Petar Stoyanov warned that his country may not be able to honour its debts without international help.
"I think when the market reassessed his comments, they realised it was nothing new. Basically, it was Stoyanov taking a swipe at (Bulgarian) parliament," a U.S. bank trader said.
By late morning, IABs had steadied at 46-3/4 cents in the dollar.
There were reports that SBC Warburg had stopped market-making in Bulgarian debt but traders said it had no impact.
The bank declined to comment on the reports.

Bulgarian Bradys have fallen about 10 percent over the past week and traders said that until the economic and politicial chaos in the country looks as though it is going to be resolved prices would remain very shaky.
Protestors were stepping up strikes as part of efforts to force the ruling Socialists to hold early elections, which analysts says is probably the only way out of the current impasse.
However, the ruling party has finally set a date for talks on elections.
Russia debt had a changeable morning, opening higher only to be hit by an aggressive seller of when-and-if paper.

The rest of the market was very quiet, though there was some continuing interest in Brazil C bonds, which have been buoyed by the increasing likelihood that the constitution will be altered to allow President Henrique Cardoso to stand for a second term.
